sources.entry: ParlayAPI MCP - Connects AI assistants to sports odds, player props, public event discovery, and account usage; account data tools use each user's own API key and allowances. #mcp #freemium

summary.one_liner: An MCP server that gives AI assistants tools for ParlayAPI sports odds, player props, betting-value analysis, public live previews, and account signup.
summary.what_it_does: The server exposes ParlayAPI functions as MCP tools for clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, and OpenClaw. Several public tools need no key: signup, pricing, live sports and search, a live best-line preview, source-quality metadata, and per-book coverage proof. Keyed tools cover game odds, player props, best line per outcome, consensus odds, and arbitrage, +EV, middles, and parlay grading. The README also lists a "verdict" tool that gives a BET/PASS call, and a "best bets" tool that ranks +EV plays limited to books the user can bet at. Account tools (signup, checkout link, magic link, saved-book preferences) are described as requiring explicit approval in the client. A quickstart resource with Python and JS samples is also provided.
use_cases: Pull live sports odds and player props into an AI assistant
Find best available price across sportsbooks
Scan for arbitrage, +EV, or middle bets
Grade a multi-leg parlay before placing it
Check API account tier and remaining credits
Sign up for a free ParlayAPI key from inside a chat
how_to_run: Add a stdio server entry with command uvx and args ["parlayapi-mcp"] to your MCP client config; optionally set PARLAYAPI_KEY in env
Claude Desktop: download the -directory.mcpb bundle from the latest desktop release and open it
notable: Works keyless for discovery, signup, pricing, and coverage tools; add a key later for paid data
Signup tool can create a free-tier key (1,000 credits/mo, no card) without leaving the chat, per the README
Docker setup runs read-only with dropped capabilities and passes the key only at runtime
Tool table separates no-auth public tools from key-required account and data tools
Explicit note that the desktop bundle version and the Python package version can differ in checkout handling
caveats: Account tools use the user's own allowance; the README says to check current plans and limits
Data use is governed by ParlayAPI Terms and any written agreement; the MIT license grants no data distribution rights
The pinned 0.3.6 desktop bundle lacks the 0.3.8 checkout-ownership fix; the README says to check the release page for newer bundles
keywords: get odds for my ai agent
